agent.problem: The opening identifies the speaker and the subject, but it never says to whom Hosea is speaking. Saying that the message is about Ephraim does not identify its audience.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

agent.problem: Verse 10 also says that, despite all this, Israel does not seek the LORD. No card tells or asks about that concluding indictment; the false answer here only establishes that Israel does not return to Him.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

agent.problem: The first blank asks for redeem without any earlier setup establishing the LORD's willingness to redeem them. The preceding cards have described judgment, so supplying that unseen wording is a guess rather than a conclusion about the verse's meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: Several choice cards do not identify their subject independently. Cards 12, 15 and 17 use them or they without an antecedent; cards 13 and 14 say only the people; and card 19 depends on the phrase These are the same people. Without the earlier cards on screen, these questions do not clearly identify Ephraim or Israel.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
